subject: Clarify metering for function/tool calls & JSON output
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@finbank.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@finbank.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rate card questions — function calls & JSON mode

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked how Redwood handled routing and the latency profiles. Procurement asked me to capture a few concrete pricing clarifications before we move to MCN. Can you confirm the following?

1) Function/tool calling: does Redwood meter and bill the same way as normal text generation tokens, or is there an additional per-call charge (e.g., for orchestrating external tool invocations)? If there is an extra fee, can you provide the unit economics and an example calculation for an average flow (prompt 120 tokens, function call payload 450 tokens returned, 3 calls per user session)?

2) Structured output / JSON mode: is there any separate metering for structured output generation (we often receive machine-readable JSON and want to ensure we aren’t double-billed for formatting or post-processing tokens). If you have a short table showing how a 1,000 session batch would be billed under standard vs. JSON-mode, that would help.

3) Caching / deduping: do cached function outputs reduce billed tokens or are they considered stored artifacts with separate billing?

We attached our procurement questionnaire (procurement_qs.pdf) — procurement will run the numbers and then we can sync. Early preference is for a committed-usage discount if we can get predictable unit pricing.

Appreciate the quick clarification — can you respond within 48 hrs?

Best,
Alyssa
Director, AI Integrations
FinBank

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Rate card questions — function calls & JSON mode

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the clear list and for sending the questionnaire. Quick answers up front, and I’ve attached a short rate card + worked example sheet for the exact calculations.

1) Function/tool calling: by default we bill for all tokens generated/consumed (prompt + model output + function payloads). There is an optional small per-tool-call orchestration surcharge (default 0.05 USD per external tool invocation) for Hosted customers that use our managed connectors — this covers network, retries, and logging. If you self-host connectors or pipe responses directly to your infra via our Private offering, that surcharge can be waived.

2) JSON/structured output: there is no separate formatting fee. Metering is token-based: the JSON body tokens are billed the same as any generated tokens. Note that structured outputs can increase token counts because of syntactic tokens (braces, field names) and quoting. In the attached workbook (function-calling-metering.xlsx) I included examples: a 1,000-session batch with your average sizes increases billed tokens by ~12% in JSON mode vs. free-text mode in our sample prompts.

3) Caching: cached responses stored in Redwood’s managed prefix cache reduce billed tokens when served from cache — we do not bill token generation for cache hits. However, we do charge a small storage-and-retrieval fee for long-term cached artifacts under the Dedicated/Private retention add-on.

Discounts: we regularly offer committed monthly token tiers with stepped discounts. For Hosted API customers we can provide a 12-month commit with a 15–25% discount depending on volume. I included a baseline rate card (redwood-ratecard-v2.pdf) with the per-1k-token prices and a worked example for the function-calling scenario you described.

Would you like a short call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet and a tailored offer? If procurement prefers, we can also run a 2-week pilot with actual traffic to produce precise cost projections.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Camila — thanks for the fast reply and the attachments. A couple follow-ups after scanning the workbook:

• The 0.05 USD per-call surcharge is clear. Can you confirm whether that surcharge applies when the function response is small (<128 tokens) vs large (>1k tokens)? Our flows include both.

• For caching: what qualifies as a cache hit? If we cache normalized JSON payloads in our layer and call Redwood only for initial generation, do you still consider the tokens produced earlier as billable on subsequent reads?

• Discounting mechanics: procurement prefers simple unit economics (e.g., price per 1k tokens after discounts, with any per-call fees called out separately). Can you provide two packaged options: (A) Hosted — 12mo commit + volume-based discount and (B) Hosted — pilot + month-to-month with higher per-token pricing but waived per-call surcharge for months 1–2? We want to present both to leadership.

If possible please make the math for a sample month with 3M generated tokens and 150k function calls.

Thanks — we’ll try to get procurement on a quick call Thursday.

—Alyssa

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>

Team — forwarding FinBank’s follow-ups. They want two packaged options and a worked example for 3M tokens + 150k function calls. Suggest the following for negotiation:

Proposal A (12mo commit):
- Baseline rate: $8.50 / 1k tokens (hosted standard)
- Commit: 3M tokens/month -> 20% discount -> $6.80 / 1k tokens
- Per-call orchestration surcharge: waived for enterprise commit (so $0.00 per call)
- Structured/JSON: billed at same per-token rate (no extra fees)
- Pilot credits: 250k free tokens in month 1 for verification

Proposal B (Pilot / month-to-month):
- Baseline rate: $9.75 / 1k tokens
- No long-term commit; per-call surcharge applies at $0.05 / call, but waive for first 2 months as a pilot concession
- Offer one free performance tuning session and a 30-day evaluation window

Rationale: giving them a clean per-1k unit for leadership, removing operational friction (waive per-call for the committed option) should get procurement positive. If they press on price, I’m comfortable going to 22% discount at 6M+ commit.

Can you both confirm the math (I already used the workbook but want ops to verify there’s no hidden storage/retention fees for the cache hit assumptions)? Also we should approve the DocuSign template to include the per-call waiver clause.

—Camila

From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>

Cc: ProcureOps <procureops@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Subject: Final offer & worked example for FinBank — function calls + JSON mode

Hi Alyssa — thanks for the follow-ups. Per our internal review (cc’d Rishi for legal/finance), here’s a concise, leadership-ready summary plus the worked example attached.

Summary (two options):
A) Hosted — 12mo commit (recommended)
 - Committed volume: 3M tokens/month
 - Effective price: $6.80 / 1k tokens (20% discount off list)
 - Per-call orchestration surcharge: waived for the duration of the 12mo commit
 - Pilot: 250k free tokens in month 1
 - JSON mode: billed at token rate; we estimate +12% tokens vs free-text for your current flows (see workbook)

B) Hosted — Pilot / Month-to-month
 - No long-term commit; $9.75 / 1k tokens
 - Per-call surcharge: $0.05 / call (waived months 1–2 for pilot)
 - One performance tuning session included

Worked example (monthly) — your numbers: 3,000,000 generated tokens + 150,000 function calls, average function payload 450 tokens:
 - Token billable total (base): 3,000,000 tokens
 - Function payload tokens added: 150,000 calls * 450 tokens = 67,500,000 tokens (these are billable when not cached)
 - Estimated cache hit rate: 70% (you indicated many repeated payloads) -> cached hits reduce billable function tokens to 30% of payload: 0.30 * 67,500,000 = 20,250,000 tokens
 - Total billable tokens = 3,000,000 + 20,250,000 = 23,250,000 tokens -> 23,250 * (per-1k price)

Pricing math A) 23,250 * $6.80 = $158,100 / month (with per-call surcharge waived)
Pricing math B) 23,250 * $9.75 = $226,687.50 / month + (150,000 * $0.05) if per-call surcharge applies = $7,500 -> $234,187.50 (pilot months 1–2 would waive the surcharge)

Next steps: if A looks good, we’ll issue a Docusign with the committed tier and the per-call waiver clause. If you prefer B, we’ll provision pilot keys and schedule a tuning call. I attached the same rate card and workbook with the exact cell references used for the math.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement and finance to walk through line-by-line.

Best,
